Finding first-touch grading: **hold** → `pm:on-hold` (`finding` removed, same write); `domain:identity` (the columns live in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/`); type Task.

Hold record (2026-08-16, graded by the triage seat — seat grading, not a maintainer ruling):
- **Reason**: the disposition here is the ADR-0049 three-way (enforce / `experimental` / remove) on a compliance-adjacent declared surface, and open decision card **#9054** is currently asking the maintainer exactly how this class — platform-object row columns on security objects with no liveness ledger — is to be governed. Grading this instance before that ruling would either pre-empt it or need re-doing under it.
- **Named restart condition**: the maintainer's ruling lands on **#9054**. Whichever seat records that ruling should re-open this card's grading in the same round (it is named in a cross-reference comment on #9054), applying the ruled mechanism; absent a class-level mechanism, the instance default per the #8535 precedent is *withdraw the claim in prose* rather than build recertification nobody has pull for.
- **Not** `needs-user-decision`: the decision already has a live anchor (#9054); a second card asking the same class question would duplicate the inbox entry.

Hold released → `pm:queue` (type Task). The named restart condition — the #9054 ruling — **fired 13:03Z today**: ruled Option A (no ledger is built; ⛔ Option C permanently off the table), and the ruling itself directs that this card be re-graded on its own merits as an **enforce-or-remove instance**, not a ledger question.

Re-graded scope accordingly: `last_certified_at` / `certified_by` on both grant tables are declared-with-zero-producers-and-zero-readers. Work the ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove decision for this pair concretely — either something writes/reads them (D5 recertification actually implemented, which is a feature and would need its own appetite ⇒ if the implementer lands there, that is a fork to escalate, not to build), or the columns retire through the standard removal route with its ledger/registry discipline. Removal is the expected outcome absent new pull; the `spec-property-retirement` playbook's platform-object-row analog applies.

Dispatch note: re-verify both columns are still producer-less on the merged ref at claim time (`git grep` the pair on `origin/main`) — #9054's enumeration is from 08-16 morning.

Triage: this comment comes from the triage seat Routine; not a claim.

**Claim + ruling** — PM dispatch seat, session `session_01Y26DJEHSBhhAQ6wwfsHNza`, branch `claude/issue-9046-d5-recertification-claim`.

### ✅ Restart condition discharged, verified not assumed

The body opens `Restart-when: closed #9054`. **#9054 is closed** — `not_planned`, 2026-08-16T13:05Z. ⇒ This card is live. (Its closure also settles the wider question: ⛔ no ledger is being built over platform-object row columns, so this instance gets an instance-level answer, not a governance one.)

### Ruled: **withdraw the claim in the descriptions.** ⛔ Not enforce, ⛔ not remove.

The card calls the three-way "a real question rather than a foregone one" — and then names the precedent that settles it. I am taking that steer:

> the closest precedent points at *withdraw the claim* rather than *build the feature*: for `sys_capability.active` the maintainer ruled (2026-08-13, **#8535**) that putting the capability registry on the authorization hot path was an architectural change needing its own designed card, so **the false promise was withdrawn in the prose instead.**

**⛔ Not "enforce."** That means building access recertification — a SOX/ISO access-review feature. ⭐ Real work, **zero measured pull**, and ⛔ a finding card is not where a compliance feature gets scoped. If it is ever wanted, it is its own designed card and these columns are already shaped for it.

**⛔ Not "remove."** Dropping shipped columns costs a migration over existing rows and buys nothing that the prose fix does not: the harm here is **the promise**, not the storage. Removal also drags in an ADR-0087 conversion question the card itself flags as conditional. ⚠️ Reversibility runs the right way too — a description is one line to change back if recertification is built; a dropped-and-re-added column is churn.

⇒ **The deliverable is that the two field descriptions stop asserting a capability the platform does not have.**

### Why this is worth doing rather than shrugging at

⚠️ This is a **compliance** surface, which is what makes the misreading expensive:

> A `Last Certified At` column with a description promising it records a recertification review tells an admin — **and tells an AI agent authoring against this model** — that access recertification is a thing the platform does. It is not.

⭐ And the timing sharpens it: we shipped read/view audit today (#8992) for a regulated-industry buyer. Someone doing a compliance walkthrough of `plugin-security`'s objects will meet these two columns in exactly that frame, and *"Reviewer who last attested this grant"* reads as evidence of a control that does not exist.

### Binding for the implementation

- ⛔ **Do not add a producer or a consumer.** No stamping, no staleness read, no surface.
- The rewritten descriptions must say plainly that the columns are **declared for a future recertification workflow and are not written or read by anything today** — ⛔ not softened into ambiguity. A description that merely stops promising, without saying it is inert, leaves the next reader to re-derive this card.
- ⚠️ The **generated i18n bundles** (`translations/*.objects.generated.ts`, four locales) carry these strings. ⛔ They are generated — regenerate, do not hand-edit, and confirm all four locales moved.
- ⚠️ The card's negative claim is scoped **to this repo**. ⛔ Do not restate it as absolute: an `objectui` designer preview rendering these columns would be a consumer under the 2026-08-10 ruling — though still not enforcement, and still not a producer for a value nothing writes.

⭐ **Verify the premise before writing.** The card is from 2026-08-16 and its whole basis is a whole-tree negative — that the only occurrences are the two declarations, the generated bundles, and CHANGELOG prose. Re-run that sweep on current `main`. If a producer or consumer now exists, **stop and report with the measurement**; a falsified premise reported is a full delivery.

**Landed and verified on `main`** — PR #9669 merged at 15:19:46Z.

Probed the merged tree on both objects, control + anti-control:

| probe | `sys_user_permission_set` | `sys_user_position` |
|:---|:---:|:---:|
| `grep -c '\[#9046\]'` — the measurement comment is there | `1` ✅ | `1` ✅ |
| `grep -c 'Null = never certified'` — **must be 0** | `0` ✅ | `0` ✅ |

The anti-control is the one that matters here. This card's whole deliverable is the *withdrawal* of a claim, so a new paragraph appearing alongside a surviving `Null = never certified` would read as done while still shipping the false sentence in the field help text and all four locale bundles. Both are gone. The replacement keeps the `[ADR-0091 D5]` citation and states the inertness outright — *"Reserved for a future access-recertification workflow…"* — rather than merely omitting the promise, which is the distinction the card asked for.

### Why prose, restated for the record

ADR-0049 enforce-or-remove, settled the way `sys_capability.active` was: enforcement means building a SOX/ISO access-review feature with **zero measured pull**, removal costs a migration over existing rows and buys nothing the prose fix does not. The harm was the promise, not the storage — and reversibility runs the right way, since a description is one line to change back if D5 is ever implemented.

### One thing this card produced that outlives it

The PR could not satisfy my own dispatch fence (*"regenerate the locales, do not hand-edit"*) — and measured **why** instead of working around it: extraction merges against the committed bundles and only the default locale is filled from schema labels, so a locale already holding a hand translation is deliberately never overwritten, and `--fill=default` skips a stale-but-present string because it is not a gap. Every generator-only option was worse than editing the three `help` leaves in place.

That exposed a gap worth more than this card: **nothing propagates a corrected source description into an already-translated locale, and `check:i18n` cannot see the difference** — it proves keys are in sync, never that a translated value still means what its source says. Same shape as the class this card belongs to, one layer over. Filed unassigned as **#9672** rather than left in a PR comment, because a locale bundle asserting a withdrawn compliance promise in three of four languages is exactly the failure this card existed to stop.

Also filed from this work: **#9671** — `content/docs/permissions/authorization.mdx:296` groups `reason`, `delegated_from` and the D5 pair as one set of "lifecycle-audit columns"; the first two are enforced, the D5 pair is not.
